points.description: States that Bligh's theory makes NO DISTINCTION between horizontal and vertical creep (seepage path) lengths, i.e. both are treated as equally effective in the total creep length.
points.partial_credit: 0.75 if only says it does not distinguish/treats creep lengths alike without naming horizontal and vertical, or names both but the relationship is only partly stated

points.description: Correctly uses the technical term 'creep length' (path of seepage along the base of the structure) for the lengths that are not distinguished, with horizontal and vertical both named.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the statement that Bligh's theory makes no distinction between horizontal and vertical creep lengths, with the term creep length and both directions named. Part marks only if the no-distinction idea is clear but horizontal/vertical is not named precisely. Any other drawback (e.g. ignoring uplift pressure, exit gradient, or safety against piping) or a wrong extra claim earns 0.
